summary: Aroostook County, ME tower site registered 2008; the register places it in Washburn and marks it gone. No build, staffing or present-day site details found.

facts.status_note: The Maine list marks the tower Gone; the detail page says it was located in Washburn, Maine, in the past tense
facts.elevation: 933 ft (284 m), per the register's detail page

events.note: Registered September 15, 2008, on the nomination of Bob Spear

evidence.supports: tower was located in Washburn, Maine
evidence.quote: This tower was located in Washburn, Maine.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Maine list spells the site Storey Hill; the detail page says Story Hill Tower Site. The story uses the detail page spelling and notes the list spelling.
The detail page gives N 46.800590° W 068.233330°; the Maine list gives 46.80255, -68.24990. The record keeps the detail page values, which match the brief, and the story calls both approximate.

The brief says Story Hill and another site share a register number. The only shared part found is the ME 6 suffix, which Deboullie Mountain (NHLR US 138) also carries. The US numbers differ, so the register numbers are not shared.

sources.title: Former Fire Lookout Sites, Maine list

notes_for_editor: Only two register pages could be read. Neither gives a build date, watchmen, fires, or present-day condition, so the story leaves those out and says no source describes the site today. A Facebook search snippet (Forest Fire Lookout Association, Maine chapter) describes a 1950 tower in Wade, not Washburn, but the Facebook page returned no readable text, so nothing from it is used and the Washburn/Wade difference is unresolved. The anyplaceamerica directory returned HTTP 403. The brief's 'share a register number' note is answered in resolved_conflicts. Used 3 websearch.py calls, one over the per-tower budget of 2, and about 6 page reads.
